messages:
Alina (People Ops): FYI we're getting requests for a recurring 'short-term abroad' pattern (e.g., 7-14 days/month in EU). Need clarity on WFH stipend, payroll withholding, and equipment shipping. Anyone seen this pattern before?

Marco (Eng): Planning 10 days/month in Barcelona for the next 4 months to work with a partner team. Do I keep full stipend or get prorated? Also concerned about laptops crossing borders.

Jin (Finance): High level: if homebase doesn't change (no >90 consecutive days), benefits stay tied to homebase. Stipend is typically prorated by days not at homebase unless there's a business need approved by Finance+Manager.

Clara (Legal): Cross-border note: repeated presence abroad raises payroll, VAT, and immigration flags. If any customer-facing, hiring, or contracting work happens there, escalate. Also, devices crossing borders may trigger temporary import rules; keep receipts and serials.

Alina (People Ops): Proposed interim rule: default proration by calendar days away: payout = (homebase_days / total_days_in_month) * monthly_stipend. Employees can request full stipend with manager + Finance justification (e.g., company-paid coworking seat).

Marco (Eng): Example: 10 days away in a 30-day month  what's the payout if stipend=$200?

Jin (Finance): Math: homebase_days=20 -> payout = (20/30)*200 = $133.33 -> round to $133. We'll show any nonresident withholding notes on your paystub.

Alina (People Ops): Process: 1) open People Ops case with exact dates, city/country, and list any local business activities; 2) confirm if coworking will be billed to you or vendor; 3) indicate if you need IT to ship hardware. Target response 3 business days.

PeopleOps-Bot: Case created #39822 "Marco - Barcelona 10d/mo". Alina will triage.

Marco (Eng): If IT ships a loaner to Barcelona, any paperwork needed?

IT-Logistics: We need People Ops approval then an IT ticket. For international shipments we require device serials, invoice copy, and confirmation of return shipping plan. You may be asked to sign a custody acknowledgment.

Clara (Legal): Also flag on cases: if you'll be interviewing or meeting vendors there, note it. Recruiting or contractual negotiations elevate nexus risk and may require pre-approval.

Alina (People Ops): Final note: submit cases at least 10 business days before first travel so Finance can calculate payroll adjustments. We'll draft an FAQ and an "international short-stay addendum" and post the link here when ready. Thanks all :white_check_mark:
